notes.claim: A body keeps its motion at constant velocity unless a net external force acts, so constant velocity means zero net force, not a force pushing it along.
Acceleration is proportional to the net external force in the same direction and, as the full law states, inversely proportional to mass, so a net force changes velocity.

sources.title: 5.2 Newton's First Law - University Physics Volume 1 | OpenStax — OpenStax
sources.quote: A body at rest remains at rest or, if in motion, remains in motion at constant velocity unless acted on by a net external force.

sources.title: 4.2 Newton's First Law of Motion: Inertia - Physics | OpenStax — OpenStax
sources.quote: According to Newton’s first law of motion, any object moving at constant velocity has no net external force acting upon it, which means that the sum of the forces acting on the object must be zero.

sources.title: 5.3 Newton's Second Law - University Physics Volume 1 | OpenStax — OpenStax
sources.quote: The acceleration of a system is directly proportional to and in the same direction as the net external force acting on the system

sources.title: 5.3 Newton's Second Law - University Physics Volume 1 | OpenStax — OpenStax
sources.quote: A change in velocity means, by definition, that there is acceleration.
